events.title: The Second Council of Lyons opens
events.shortBlurb: The fourteenth ecumenical council gathered to seek reunion with the Greeks and reform of the Church…
body: On 7 May 1274 Gregory X opened the Second Council of Lyons, reckoned the fourteenth general council of the Church, in the cathedral of St. John. Some five hundred bishops attended, with envoys of the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos and of the Western princes; James I of Aragon came in person.

The council had three ends: aid for the Holy Land, the reform of the Church, and reunion with the Greeks. On 6 July the emperor's envoys accepted the Latin faith, and union between East and West was solemnly proclaimed; it did not outlive the decade, being repudiated at Constantinople after Michael's death.

To end the long vacancies of the papal see, the constitution Ubi Periculum bound the cardinals to strict enclosure in conclave. Thomas Aquinas had died in March on the road to Lyons; Bonaventure, who guided much of the council's work, died there on 15 July, two days before it closed.
